exact_statement: For k >= 3, let F_k(n) be the minimum number of colours needed to colour an n-vertex graph with floor(n^2/4)+1 edges so that every C_(2k+1) is rainbow. For k=3, prove or refute that F_3(n) is asymptotic to n^2/8.
scope_notes: Round 8 proved a 12+4+4+1 singleton-kernel formula only for one locked 16-vertex natural-switch assignment.

Round 9 asks whether the same five-block kernel, or a nontrivial parameterized necessary subkernel, follows from the natural-switch architecture for arbitrary block sizes; alternatively an exact parameterized counterbranch may refute that lift.
A counterbranch must be specified for infinitely many parameter values and proved by explicit cycle templates or a complete symbolic reduction; another finite census does not count.
Even a parameterized theorem for this architecture does not imply the public F_3(n)~n^2/8 statement without an all-hard-branch reduction.
